μετ' ὀλίγα· Ἐὰν ᾖς ἁμαρτωλὸς, ἐὰν ᾖς πόρνος, ἐὰν καταφερὴς, οὐ διορισθήσῃ ἀπὸ
τῶν τετραπόδων. Ἵπποι θηλυμανεῖς ἐγεννήθησαν. ∆ιὰ τοῦτο θαῤῥῶν λέγει, ὅτι
ἐχωρίσθη· Ὁ διορίζων με ἀπὸ τετραπόδων γῆς. ΚΕΦ. Μʹ. Στίχ. γʹ. Μὴ, ἀλλὰ ζῶσαι
ὥσπερ ἀνὴρ τὴν ὀσφύν σου. ∆ίδωμί σοι παῤῥησίαν. Ἐγώ σε ἐρωτήσω· σὺ δέ μοι
ἀπόκριναι. Ἤδη ἆθλον αὐτῷ δίδωσιν ὁ Θεός. Ἄνθρωπον ἐρωτᾷ, ὅτι πυνθάνεται
αὐτοῦ, ὅτι δίδωσιν ἐξουσίαν τῆς ἀποκρίσεως. Εἰ μὴ ἦν νενικηκὼς, οὐκ ἂν ἐλάμβα
νεν· εἰ μὴ ἦν ὑπομείνας, οὐκ ἂν ἤκουσε· Ζῶσαι ὥσπερ ἀνὴρ τὴν ὀσφύν σου.
Ἐρωτήσω δέ σε· σὺ δέ μοι ἀπόκριναι. Τοῦ αὐτοῦ. Μὴ πρότερον ἀποκρινάσθω τις τῷ
Θεῷ, ἐὰν μὴ, γενόμενος ἀνὴρ, ζώσηται ὥσπερ ἀνὴρ τὴν ὀσφὺν αὐτοῦ. Ὅσον γὰρ ἡ
ὀσφὺς αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἔζω σται, ἀλλὰ λέλυται, καὶ οὐχὶ περιδέδεται, οὐδὲ συν έσφιγκται,
οὐ δύναται εὐλόγως ἀποκρίνασθαι τῷ Κυρίῳ. Στίχ. γʹ. Ἐρωτήσω δέ σε· σὺ δέ μοι
ἀποκρίθητι. Τὰ μὲν τέλεια τῶν ἀγωνισμάτων τοῖς καλῶς ἀθλή σασι μετὰ τὸν βίον
ἀπόκειται τοῦτον. Οὐδὲν δὲ ἧττον καὶ ἤδη ἡ χάρις ἡ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀῤῥαβωνίζεται τοὺς
ἀθλητάς. ∆ιὰ τοῦτο, ὅτε ἠγωνίσατο τὰ μέγιστα ὁ Ἰώβ· ὅτε, ἀποβαλὼν τὰ ὑπάρχοντα,
ἐδόξασε τὸν δεδωκότα· ὅτε, ἀποθέμενος τὰ τέκνα, ηὐχαρίστησε τῷ παρειλη φότι·
ὅτε, νοήσας ὡς σκώληκας ἀνάγειν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ σώματος, οὐ νενίκηται ἀπὸ τῶν
πόνων· προοίμια καὶ ἀῤῥαβῶνα τῶν ἀθλητῶν δίδωσιν αὐτῷ ὁ Θεὸς, χρηματίσας
αὐτῷ διὰ λαίλαπος καὶ νεφῶν. Ἀκούσας οὖν προτέρων λόγων, δέον ἀποκρίνασθαι
πρὸς Θεὸν, σιωπᾷ, ὡς οὐκ ἔχων παῤῥησίαν ἀποκρίνασθαι πρὸς αὐτόν. Οὔπω γὰρ ᾔδει
τὸ ὕστερον γεγραμμένον ὑπὸ Μωϋσέως, ὡς Μωϋσῆς ἐλάλει, ὁ δὲ Θεὸς ἀπεκρί νατο
αὐτῷ φωνῇ. Ὡς μὴ ἐπιστάμενος τοίνυν τοῦτο, οὐ θέλει ἀποκρίνασθαι πρὸς τὸν Θεόν.
Ὁ δὲ Θεὸς δί δωσιν αὐτῷ παῤῥησίαν τοῦ λαλεῖν. Καὶ μεθ' ἕτερα· Τοσαύτη ἐστὶν ἡ
χρηστότης τοῦ Θεοῦ, ὥστε ἀναλα βεῖν αὐτὸν πρόσωπον οὐ κρίνοντος, ἀλλὰ
κρινομένου μετὰ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου. Καὶ πολλαὶ τοῦτο ἐδίδαξαν Γρα φαί. ∆εῦτε, καὶ
διαλεχθῶμεν, λέγει Κύριος. Καὶ, Λαός μου, μᾶλλον δὲ ὁ Θεὸς μετὰ τοῦ λαοῦ
διαλεχθή σεται, λαός μου, τί ἐποίησά σοι, ἢ τί παρηνόχλησά σοι; ἀποκρίθητί μοι, καὶ
τὰ ἑξῆς. Στίχ. γʹ. Μὴ ἀποποιοῦ μου τὸ κρῖμα. Μὴ ἀποποιοῦ μου τοῦτο τὸ κρῖμα.
Τούτου τοῦ ῥητοῦ ὡς χρησίμου μνημονεύσωμεν. Ἀλλ' ὅτ' ἂν κρίνῃ ὁ Θεὸς παθεῖν τι
ἡμᾶς, τέκνον ἀποβαλεῖν, ἄρ χοντα ἀπολέσαι, νοσῆσαι κατὰ τὸ σῶμα, ὅ τι δήποτε
τούτων ὑπομεῖναι· οὐδὲν τούτων οἷόν τέ ἐστιν ἡμᾶς παθεῖν, μὴ κρίνοντος τοῦ Θεοῦ.
Οὐδὲ γὰρ στρουθίον πίπτει εἰς παγίδα ἄνευ βουλήματος τοῦ Πατρὸς, τοῦ ἐν τοῖς
οὐρανοῖς. Ἐπεὶ οὖν οὐδὲν τούτων γίνεται χω ρὶς κρίματος τοῦ Θεοῦ, λέγεται πρὸς
τὸν παθόντα· 17.100 Μὴ ἀποποιοῦ μου τὸ κρῖμα, μὴ ἀπαρνῇ, ὅτι ἔκρινα περὶ σοῦ.
Στίχ. γʹ. Οἴει δέ με ἄλλως σοι κεχρηματικέναι, ἢ ἵνα ἀναφανῇς δίκαιος; Ἀπολογοῦμαί
σοι. ∆ίκαιος ἦς, ἀλλ' οὐκ ἦς φανε ρός. Ὑπομονὴν εἶχες· ἔδει με ἀφορμὴν παρασχεῖν
τοῦ λάμψαι σου τὴν ὑπομονήν. Εἶχες ἀνδρείαν· ἀλλ' ἐκέκρυπτο ἐν σοί· οἱ
συμβεβηκότες πόνοι ἔδειξάν σου τὴν ἀνδρείαν. Καὶ μετ' ὀλίγα· Μνημονεύωμεν τού
των ἐν τοῖς περιστάσεων καιροῖς, καὶ δόξωμεν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀκούειν παρόντος, καὶ
λέγοντος ἡμῖν· Οἴει δέ με ἄλλως σοι κεχρηματικέναι, ἢ ἵνα ἀναφανῇς δίκαιος; Μὴ
ἀναφανῶμεν ἄδικοι, μηδὲ ἀσεβεῖς. Στίχ. εʹ. Ἀνάλαβε δὴ ὕψος καὶ δύναμιν.
Στεφάνωσαι, ἔνδυσαι δόξαν, ἔνδυσαι τιμήν. Στίχ. ʹ. Ἀπόστειλον δὲ ἀγγέλους ὀργῇ·
πάντα δὲ ὑβριστὴν ταπείνωσον. Στίχ. ζʹ. Ὑπερήφανον δὲ σβέσον. Ὁ ὑβριστὴς
ἐστρατεύσατο κατὰ σοῦ. Εἶπέ μοί πο τε ὁ ὑβριστὴς, Ἀπόστειλον τὴν χεῖρά σου· εἶπέ
μοι, Ἅψαι πάντων ὧν ἔχει· εἶπέ μοι περὶ σοῦ, ὡς ἄρα εἰς πρόσωπόν με εὐλογήσεις.
Ἀλλ' οὖν γε νε νίκηκας. ∆ιὰ τοῦτό σοι λέγω· Θάῤῥει· πᾶν δὲ ὑβρι στὴν ταπείνωσον,
καὶ τοὺς ἀγγέλους αὐτοῦ ταπείνω σον. Ὑπερήφανος ἐκεῖνος γεγένηται κατὰ σοῦ·
ἀλλὰ σὺ ὑπερήφανον σβέσον. Ἀσεβὴς ἐκεῖνος κατὰ σοῦ· ἀλλὰ σὺ σκῆψον ἀσεβεῖς
παραχρῆμα. Στίχ. ηʹ. Τὰ δὲ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν ἀτιμίας πλήρωσον. Ἔλεγξον
ἁμαρτωλοὺς, δεικνὺς αὐτοὺς ἁμαρτωλούς. Πλήρωσον τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν ἀτιμίας
διὰ τοῦ ἐλέγ χου τοῦ ἐν σοί. Στίχ. ιʹ. Ἀλλὰ δὴ ἰδοὺ θηρία παρὰ σοί· χόρτον ἶσα βουσὶν
ἐσθίει. Θηρία αἱ ἀντικείμεναι δυνάμεις εἰσὶ, περὶ ὧν ηὔ ξατο ὁ Προφήτης λέγων· Μὴ
παραδῷς τοῖς θηρίοις τὴν ψυχὴν ἐξομολογουμένην σοι. Θηρία εἰσὶν αἱ ἀντικείμεναι
δυνάμεις, ὧν εἴληφας, ὦ ἄνθρωπε, τὴν ἐξουσίαν. Ἐὰν Θεῷ δουλεύσῃς, ἐπ' ἀσπίδα
pass_a_gloss: …a little later: if you are a sinner, if you are a fornicator, if lustful, you will not be separated from the four-footed. Horses mad for females were born (became). Because of this, being confident, he says that he was separated: the one separating me from four-footed of earth. Chapter 40, verse 3 (catena numbering). No, but gird like a man your loin. I give you freedom of speech. I will ask you; and you answer me. Already God gives him a prize. He asks a man, in that he inquires of him, in that he gives authority of the answer. If he had not conquered, he would not have received; if he had not endured, he would not have heard: Gird like a man your loin. And I will ask you; and you answer me. Of the same. Let no one first answer God, unless, having become a man, he girds like a man his loin. For as long as his loin has not been girded, but has been loosed, and not bound around, nor drawn together, he cannot reasonably answer the Lord. Verse 3. And I will ask you; and you answer me. The perfect things of the contests are laid up for those having competed well after this life. But nothing less also already the grace of God gives a pledge to the athletes. Because of this, when Job had contested the greatest things; when, having thrown away the possessions, he glorified the one having given; when, having put off the children, he gave thanks to the one having taken; when, perceiving as it were to bring up worms from his body, he was not conquered by the toils; preludes and a pledge of the athletes God gives him, having spoken oracularly to him through whirlwind and clouds. Having heard then earlier words, it being needed to answer toward God, he is silent, as not having freedom of speech to answer toward him. For not yet did he know the thing later written by Moses, how Moses was speaking, and God answered him by a voice. As not knowing this then, he does not want to answer toward God. But God gives him freedom of speech of speaking. And after other things: So great is the kindness of God, so as for him to take up a face (role) not of one judging, but of one being judged with the man. And many Scriptures taught this. Come and let us converse, says the Lord. And: My people, or rather God will converse with the people, my people, what did I do to you, or how did I trouble you? Answer me, and the following. Verse 3. Do not reject my judgment. Do not reject this judgment of mine. Of this saying as useful let us make remembrance. But whenever God judges us to suffer something, to throw away a child, to lose a ruler, to be sick according to the body, to endure whatever of these; none of these is possible for us to suffer, God not judging. For not even a sparrow falls into a snare without the will of the Father, the one in the heavens. Since then none of these comes to be apart from judgment of God, it is said toward the one having suffered: Do not reject my judgment, do not deny that I judged about you. Verse 3. And do you think me to have dealt oracularly with you otherwise, than that you might appear righteous? I make a defense to you. You were righteous, but you were not manifest. You had endurance; it was needed for me to provide a starting point for your endurance to shine. You had courage; but it had been hidden in you; the toils that happened showed your courage. And after a little: Let us remember these things in the times of circumstances, and let us seem to hear God being present and saying to us: Do you think me to have dealt with you otherwise, than that you might appear righteous? Let us not appear unrighteous, nor impious. Verse 5. Take up then height and power. Crown yourself, put on glory, put on honour. Verse 6 (numeral lost). And send out angels in wrath; and humble every insolent one. Verse 7. And quench a proud one. The insolent one made campaign against you. The insolent one once said to me: send out your hand; he said to me: touch all things which he has; he said to me about you, that indeed you will bless me to my face. But nevertheless you have conquered. Because of this I say to you: take courage; humble every insolent one, and humble his angels. That one has become proud against you; but you quench a proud one. That one is impious against you; but you strike the impious immediately. Verse 8. And fill their faces with dishonour. Convict sinners, showing them sinners. Fill their faces with dishonour through the conviction which is in you. Verse 10. But indeed behold beasts beside you; grass equal to oxen it eats. Beasts are the opposing powers, about which the Prophet prayed saying: do not hand over to the beasts the soul confessing to you. Beasts are the opposing powers, of which you have received, O man, the authority. If you serve God, upon an asp…
pass_b_english: … a little later: If you are a sinner, if you are a fornicator, if you are given to lust, you will not be separated from the four-footed beasts. “They became horses mad for mares” (Jeremiah 5:8). That is why he says with confidence that he has been set apart: “He who separates me from the four-footed beasts of the earth” (Job 35:11).

“No; but gird your loins like a man” (Job 40:7). I give you freedom of speech: I will ask you, and you answer me. God is already giving him a prize. He questions a man, in that he inquires of him, in that he gives him the right to answer. Had he not conquered, he would not have received this; had he not endured, he would not have heard: “Gird your loins like a man; I will ask you, and you answer me.”

From the same: Let no one answer God before he has become a man and girded his loins like a man. For as long as his loins are not girded, but slack, not bound round or drawn tight, he cannot fittingly answer the Lord.

“I will ask you, and you answer me” (Job 40:7). The full rewards of the contests are stored up, after this life, for those who have fought well. Yet even now, no less, the grace of God gives the athletes a pledge. That is why, when Job had fought the greatest fights; when he had lost his possessions and glorified the one who had given them; when he had put his children from him and given thanks to the one who had taken them; when he saw that he was, as it were, bringing up worms from his body and was not overcome by his pains: then God gives him the first-fruits and the pledge that belong to athletes, speaking to him through whirlwind and clouds. So when he had heard the earlier words, though he ought to have answered God, he keeps silent, as one who has no freedom to answer him. For he did not yet know what Moses wrote later, that “Moses spoke, and God answered him by a voice” (Exodus 19:19). Not knowing this, then, he does not want to answer God. But God gives him freedom to speak.

And after other matters: So great is the kindness of God that he takes on the role not of one who judges, but of one who goes to judgment with the man. And many Scriptures have taught this: “Come, and let us reason together, says the Lord” (Isaiah 1:18). And: “My people” (or rather, God will argue his case with the people), “my people, what have I done to you, or how have I wearied you? Answer me” (Micah 6:3), and so on.

“Do not reject my judgment” (Job 40:8). Do not reject this judgment of mine. Let us keep this saying in mind as a useful one. Whenever God judges that we should suffer something, should lose a child, should lose a ruler, should fall ill in body, should endure any one of these things whatever: none of these can happen to us unless God judges it. For not even a sparrow falls into a snare without the will of the Father in heaven (Matthew 10:29). Since, then, none of these things happens apart from God's judgment, it is said to the one who suffers: “Do not reject my judgment”: do not deny that I have judged concerning you.

“Do you think I have dealt with you for any other reason than that you might be shown to be righteous?” (Job 40:8). I am making my defense to you. You were righteous, but you were not seen to be. You had endurance; I had to give an occasion for your endurance to shine. You had courage, but it lay hidden in you; the toils that came upon you showed your courage.

And a little later: Let us remember these things in times of trouble, and let us think that we hear God present and saying to us: “Do you think I have dealt with you for any other reason than that you might be shown to be righteous?” Let us not be shown to be unrighteous, or ungodly.
“Take on, then, loftiness and power” (Job 40:10). Crown yourself; clothe yourself with glory, clothe yourself with honor.

“And send out angels in wrath, and humble every insolent one” (Job 40:11). “And quench the proud” (Job 40:12). The insolent one made war against you. The insolent one once said to me: “Put forth your hand.” He said to me: “Touch all that he has.” He said to me about you that you would surely bless me to my face (Job 1:11). But you have conquered all the same. That is why I say to you: Take courage; humble every insolent one, and humble his angels. That one became proud against you; but you, quench the proud. That one is ungodly against you; but you, strike down the ungodly at once.
“And fill their faces with dishonor” (Job 40:13). Convict sinners by showing them to be sinners. Fill their faces with dishonor through the conviction that is in you.

“But look, there are wild beasts beside you; it eats grass like oxen” (Job 40:15). The wild beasts are the opposing powers, about which the Prophet prayed, saying: “Do not hand over to the wild beasts the soul that confesses to you” (Psalm 74:19). The wild beasts are the opposing powers over which you, O man, have received authority. If you serve God, upon the asp …

choices.choice: Τοῦ αὐτοῦ -> 'From the same:'; Καὶ μεθ' ἕτερα -> 'And after other matters:'; Καὶ μετ' ὀλίγα -> 'And a little later:' (opening of the section: '… a little later:'). Each opens its own paragraph; no attribution guessed.
Catena labels converted by the words to KJV: γʹ -> 40:7/40:8, εʹ -> 40:10, ϛʹ -> 40:11, ζʹ -> 40:12, ηʹ -> 40:13, ιʹ -> 40:15.
The paraphrases in God's first person ('I give you freedom of speech', 'I am making my defense to you', 'The insolent one once said to me ... That is why I say to you') kept first person.
μᾶλλον δὲ ὁ Θεὸς μετὰ τοῦ λαοῦ διαλεχθήσεται kept as the commentator's parenthesis inside the quotation.
Put forth your hand / touch all that he has / bless me to my face: cited once after the indirect clause.
Ends 'upon the asp …' mid-sentence (Psalm 91:13 continues in u04-open).
